title: Keel's rate limits pair a maximum amount with a daily slope, capping both standing exposure and speed
content:
Every entry under A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.1.1.3 carries the same two fields, for example `LIMIT_USDS_TO_USDC` at "`maxAmount`: 100,000,000 USDS, `slope`: 50,000,000 USDS per day."

The pair encodes two different risks. `maxAmount` bounds the worst case at any instant — the most that can be outstanding if everything goes wrong at once. `slope` bounds the rate at which the budget replenishes, so an actor who exhausts a limit cannot simply repeat the operation; they must wait while capacity accrues.

That second parameter is what makes the design defensive against a compromised operator rather than merely against a large mistake. A single-parameter cap can be drained repeatedly as fast as the underlying positions can be unwound; a slope turns the maximum into a per-day flow ceiling, converting an instantaneous theft into a slow leak that humans and the Freezer role have time to notice and stop.

Because the limits are enforced by an on-chain `ALM_RATE_LIMITS` contract (A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.1.1.1.2.1.6) rather than by operator discipline, they bind even when the relayer keys are in the wrong hands — which is precisely the scenario they exist for.
description: Every limit in the Liquidity Layer is a two-parameter budget that refills over time, so a limit constrains how much can be at risk and how fast it can be reached or re-used.
